content.title: When is Artemis II launch today? Here's how to watch live stream
content.text: Updated April 1, 2026, 9:07 a.m. ETWhether you want to watch in person or via livestream, here's how you can see the launch of Artemis II today.Launch time is 6:24 p.m. ET, and there is a two-hour launch window.Can you see the launch where you live? Check the visibility map."Next stop: The moon."That was the post on X from NASA as we enter the final hours before the launch of Artemis II later today, April 1 and was followed by "The next era of exploration begins," from NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.It's been more than 50 years since we've headed toward the moon, and the Artemis missions are laying the groundwork to establish a moon base. Eventual goal? Heading to Mars.Here's where you can watch today's launch, both in person and via livestream.What time is the Artemis II launch today?Artemis II is scheduled to launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.Launch time is 6:24 p.m. ET, and there is a two-hour launch window.Artemis II countdown clockHow to watch Artemis II launch coverage, get live updatesThe USA TODAY Network Space Team will provide live updates starting at 10 a.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, at floridatoday.com/space.Live view of Artemis II on launch pad at Kennedy Space Center in FloridaUSA TODAY to live stream Artemis II launchUSA Today will begin live streaming the Artemis II moon mission and launch beginning at 9 a.m. April 1.Where else can you watch livestream of Artemis II launch?Watch livestreams on:Amazon PrimeNASA's YouTube channelNASA+Amazon Prime membershipWhat's best place to watch Artemis II launch in Florida? Can I see it where I live?The trajectory for Artemis II will be toward the east after it launches from Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral.NASA's graphic shows where where the rocket could be visible at various times after the launch.Multiple parks along the Indian River in Titusville provide a view directly across Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral launch pads but as many as 400,000 people are expected to be on the Space Coast for the launch.➤ View from Volusia County➤ View from Treasure Coast➤ View from Palm Beach County➤ View from Southwest FloridaWhere will Artemis II go?Artemis II will fly around the Earth before going around the moon inside the Orion spacecraft.The 10-day mission around the moon will send astronauts farther into space than even the Apollo missions.Will Artemis II land on the moon?No. Artemis II will fly around the moon.Artemis II will be the first crewed test flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft. The crew are testing systems and hardware ahead of a future moon landing.How tall is the SLS rocket used in Artemis II mission?NASA's Space Launch System rocket is 322 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty's 305 feet but still smaller than the 363-foot-tall Saturn V. It's also the most powerful rocket NASA has ever launched, with 8.8 million pounds of thrust.On top of the SLS rocket is the Orion crew capsule.Will we really build a moon base?NASA is looking to establish a permanent foothold on the moon's south pole, using a series of crewed and uncrewed missions in the years ahead to build a moon base before possibly venturing to Mars.Who is on board Artemis II?The four astronauts selected for the Artemis II mission include:Reid Wiseman, commanderVictor Glover, pilotChristina Koch, mission specialistCanadian Space Agency's Jeremy Hansen, mission specialist3 of 4 astronauts on Artemis II set firstsThree of the four astronauts on the Artemis II mission are setting records:first woman to venture near the moon: mission specialist Christina Kochfirst Black man to venture near the moon: pilot Victor Gloverfirst Canadian to venture near the moon: mission specialist Jeremy HansenWhat's special about Artemis II?Astronauts have not traveled beyond Earth orbit since the 1972 Apollo 17 mission.Artemis II also will be about 250,000 miles in space — farther than the record-setting Apollo 13 mission.Astronauts on board also will see sights on the far side of the moon never before seen by humans.What's weather forecast for Artemis II? 80% go for launch NASA currently forecasts an "80% chance of favorable weather condition."The National Weather Service forecast for Wednesday calls for a slight chance for showers between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. and then partly sunny skies with a high near 78. Winds will be out of the east at 5 to 15 mph. Chance of rain is 20%.Will Artemis II astronauts return to Florida?No. When they return to Earth, the astronauts in the Orion capsule will make a parachute-assisted water landing in the Pacific Ocean near California.Contributors: Rick Neale and Brooke Edwards, FLORIDA TODAY, and Eric Lagatta, USA TODAY NetworkCheryl McCloud is a journalist for the USA TODAY Network-Florida's service journalism Connect team.
